title: Dark Side of the Cinema
intro: Some films don't just disturb you, they rewire you. These are the ones that linger long after the credits roll.

films.title: Oldboy
films.line: A man walks out of captivity and straight into something far worse than imprisonment.

films.title: Frailty
films.line: A father's divine mission tears a family apart from the inside out.

films.title: Caché
films.line: Mysterious surveillance tapes arrive and slowly unravel a man's carefully constructed life.

films.title: Prisoners
films.line: Two missing girls and one desperate father push the moral limits of love.

films.title: Se7en
films.blurb: New Line's executives hated the ending and kept asking for a happier one. David Fincher was sent Andrew Kevin Walker's original script by mistake, read it, and agreed to direct only if that ending stayed. Brad Pitt dug in as well. Test audiences were lukewarm and nobody expected much, then it grossed $327 million and finished as the seventh biggest film of 1995. Two detectives, seven sins, one box.

films.title: The Vanishing
films.line: An obsession with a single unanswered question leads somewhere you will not recover from.

films.title: Hereditary
films.line: Grief cracks a family open and something ancient and merciless crawls inside.

films.title: Memories of Murder
films.line: Two detectives chase a killer through the rain and slowly lose themselves in the hunt.

films.title: Enemy
films.line: Finding your exact double should feel like a miracle, not the beginning of something unbearable.

films.title: The Invitation
films.line: A dinner party feels just a little too warm, a little too curated, a little too wrong.
